judge.rationale: The candidate accurately implements the core logic in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` by wrapping non-Error rejections in an `Error` with `cause` preserved, and updates the spec and CHANGELOG as required. For formatting the error message, the candidate uses `node:util`'s `inspect` whereas the reference uses `JSON.stringify` with a `String(error)` fallback; both handle non-Error values safely including circular objects. Instead of adding the new test to `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` like the reference (which also avoids shifting line numbers in other spec files), the candidate creates two separate test files (`onErrorCoercion.test.ts` and `onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`) and leaves a `.lore/dod.md` scratch file in the diff. Also note that `onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts` has a bare `// eslint-disable-next-line require-yield` without a description, which may trigger an eslint directive-comment rule if configured, though `onErrorCoercion.test.ts` avoids it cleanly with `yield* []`.
